known.name: Squared ReLU in the FFN (Primer)
known.mechanism: Replace ReLU with ReLU² in the feed-forward block, found by evolutionary search over transformer primitives.
known.effect: The paper reports this as the single largest gain in Primer. Primer as a whole cut training cost about 4x at 500M parameters. At 1.9B it matched the baseline's one-shot quality with roughly 1/3 of the compute.
known.where: 500M to 1.9B parameter decoder LMs on C4, T5-style comparison

known.name: ReLU² in modded-nanoGPT speedrun
known.mechanism: ReLU² replaces GELU in a non-gated MLP, bundled with padded embeddings, zero-init projections and QK-norm.
known.effect: This bundle took the record to 15.2 minutes (record log entry dated 10/14/24). ReLU² is still part of the speedrun architecture. The summary I read does not isolate its individual contribution.

known.name: ReLU² vs ReLU vs SwiGLU at matched parameters
known.mechanism: Compare ReLU, ReLU², ReGLU and SwiGLU at equal parameter counts, and measure sparsity as well as accuracy.
known.effect: Average accuracy was about 50.5 for both SwiGLU and ReLU², and 48.9 for ReLU. ReLU² gives higher activation sparsity.

known.name: GLU variants (SwiGLU, GEGLU, ReGLU)
known.mechanism: A gated MLP multiplies an activated gate projection by a linear value projection.
known.effect: SwiGLU and GEGLU gave the best perplexity among the variants tested. I did not confirm the exact numbers.

known.name: Layer-wise scaling of FFN width (OpenELM)
known.mechanism: FFN multiplier and head count grow linearly with depth, so early layers get narrower FFNs and later layers get wider ones.
known.effect: OpenELM reports a 2.36% accuracy gain over OLMo at about 1B parameters while using 2x fewer pre-training tokens. That comparison is confounded with other changes.

known.name: Layer-wise scaling variants (Crown, Frame, Reverse)
known.mechanism: Redistribute FFN width and head count across depth using 2-point or 3-point linear interpolation.
known.effect: All variants reached similar losses and beat an equal-cost uniform baseline without a large throughput drop. Larger scales are untested. One commenter reports a dtype bug in the data pipeline, which I could not verify.

known.name: Primer depthwise convolution (local mixing)
known.mechanism: Add a depthwise convolution after the Q, K and V projections to bring in local neighbor information. This sits in attention, not the MLP.
known.effect: Together with squared ReLU it forms Primer-EZ. The authors say it is easy to implement and transfers across codebases.

known.name: Shift-FFN (adjacent-token differences in the FFN)
known.mechanism: Add an adjacent-token difference term to the FFN input so the MLP sees local neighbor information. The authors say it works with GLU-style FFNs.
known.effect: Used with LoRA, it gave higher math-reasoning accuracy and fewer cyclical reasoning loops than standard LoRA or full fine-tuning. Pretraining was not tested.

known.name: Peri-LN (normalization on sublayer outputs)
known.mechanism: Apply a norm to the input and also to the output of each sublayer, as in Gemma 2 and OLMo 2. The post-MLP norm divides by the output magnitude, which bounds weight gradients.
known.effect: The authors report more stable training and bounded activation variance than Pre-LN.

known.name: Masked Gated Linear Unit (MGLU)
known.mechanism: Replace the separate gate and value matrices with one shared matrix and learned binary masks, which cuts memory reads.
known.effect: SwiMGLU matched or beat SwiGLU on downstream accuracy. The FlashMGLU kernel is 34% faster and 47% more memory-efficient than standard GLUs on an RTX5090. I did not find perplexity numbers.

failed.name: SwiGLU gave no clear gain in Falcon
failed.why: Falcon's authors saw no clear zero-shot benefit from SwiGLU at 1B and 3B, so they did not adopt it. They suggested the result depends on hyperparameter tuning.

failed.name: ReLU² does not beat SwiGLU in accuracy at matched parameters
failed.why: ReLU² only tied SwiGLU (about 50.5 each). Its advantage is sparsity and efficiency, not lower loss.

failed.name: OpenELM layer-wise scaling gain is not isolated
failed.why: OpenELM had no targeted ablation of layer-wise scaling, so its benefit is ambiguous. Follow-up work only found similar losses across variants at small scale.

open.direction: Depth-dependent FFN width, reallocating parameters between attention and MLP across the 12 layers (compare 'Reverse' and 'Crown' shapes) at 21M parameters and 50M tokens.
open.why: Existing evidence is at 180M parameters or larger, is confounded, and has not been tested at large scale. The uniform-width assumption has not been checked in a latent-attention, 4-stream-residual recipe.

open.direction: Token-shift or short causal convolution on the gated MLP input, so the MLP sees neighbor tokens, tested in pretraining.
open.why: Shift-FFN was only tested in fine-tuning. I found no pretraining ablation of a short convolution inside a SwiGLU FFN.

open.direction: Output normalization or depth-based gating of the MLP branch (Peri-LN style) in a recipe whose MLP output RMS grows to 10.9.
open.why: Peri-LN argues output norms bound variance and gradients. Its effect on loss in a mixed-stream residual with QK-norm is untested.

open.direction: ReLU² (or other sparse or polynomial) gating inside a gated MLP, replacing SiLU.
open.why: ReLU² was compared with SwiGLU only at 1.3B, with a tie on accuracy. Whether a squared activation helps the gate in a GLU at a very small token budget is not established.

open.direction: Shared-matrix or masked gating (MGLU) to buy a wider hidden size at the same parameter count.
open.why: MGLU matched SwiGLU on downstream accuracy while using fewer weight reads. Its perplexity at small scale and its use as a parameter-reallocation tool are not reported.
